files.Title: DBTools.Core.Notifications.NotificationBanner.NotificationBannerService
files.Summary: Shows transient notification banners anchored to the supplied owner through a modeless . On the owner dispatcher's thread, owner resolution and presentation run before return and their exceptions reach the caller. From any other thread the request is queued on that dispatcher, the call returns at once, and delivery failures are logged, never thrown. Choosing the dispatcher (WpfDispatcher.GetDispatcherOrThrow) can throw on any thread. A suppressed request (zero owner HWND, no anchor position, retired host, host reset) returns a handle that does nothing, so a returned handle never confirms that a banner showed. Disposing the returned handle before delivery cancels that presentation.

files.Title: DBTools.Core.Settings.Persistence.ISettingsProvider
files.Summary: Get re-reads the defaults and per-year settings files on every call (synchronous, no cache). A missing file or section, or a missing value whose member is not [JsonRequired], gives the default. A value of the wrong JSON kind at an object or collection position reads as empty, an object, array or null at a string property reads as "", and a later file's null or scalar keeps an earlier object or array. Malformed JSON, a missing [JsonRequired] member (also in an object that reads as empty), a value that does not convert at a bool or number property (null, an object or an array included) and any other I/O error throw. CommitAsync rejects an empty batch, a null entry or a repeated section, locks across processes (IOException after 10 s), re-reads the per-year file, replaces the written sections and swaps it atomically; on failure it is unchanged.

files.Title: DBTools.Presentation.ToolWindows.IToolWindowSession
files.Summary: Owns a raw-XAML view and its stable shell. Register payload event handlers and teardown through this session. Retire synchronously on the shell's UI thread before unloading a payload generation. Window and View are unavailable after retirement. ShowDialog returns null after retirement. Host-owned creation, lifecycle, root layout and dispatcher callbacks temporarily clear contextual reflection and restore the caller's scope on return. Raw templates resolve through the stable schema. The close gate, subscribed handlers and AddCleanup callbacks re-enter the creation context with ExecutionContext flow suppressed, which retirement releases on every exit. Suppression prevents captures; clearing contextual reflection controls synchronous resolution. A command must suppress flow for its entire payload reflection scope, including tool-triggered layout outside shell overrides. WPF can measure an invalidated subtree directly; that work can see the command context, but cannot capture it while flow is suppressed. Async callback continuations do not inherit that context; name resolution after an await must explicitly re-enter it under suppression for synchronous work. Binding getters/setters, edit cancellation, collection notifications and a custom shell initializer execute in the host's neutral reflection context; they must not depend on ambient name resolution.

files.Summary: The persisted identity used to decide whether one physical framing element is acted on. This deliberately contains no Revit ElementId; the owning UniqueId is supplied by the Placed record and resolved only at the model-write boundary.

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Placement.Domain.ActionSet.PlacementActionSet
files.Summary:
The single derived Update authority for acted and held identities.

Girts are always acted on. An opening row marked held (including an unframed row) keeps its physical framing untouched. This set is derived for one update from the session plan and the last successful Placed record; it is never persisted and never maintained as a second session state machine.

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Placement.Execution.PlacementOutcome
files.Summary: Domain result from a place or update run. is populated only for updates.

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Placement.Operations.ModelWrite.ModelWriteContext
files.Summary: Writer-side context for tagging, persistence, and resolved geometry. Girt and opening component writes require matching runtime-member target entries.

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Placement.Operations.ModelWrite.WallSystem.IWallSystemWriter
files.Summary: Contract for writing SGT wall aggregates to Revit. Implemented by WallSystemWriter and consumed by the placement orchestrator. Callers must already be inside a Revit API context; SGT guarantees it because SgtWindowSession.Start accepts only an InlineRevitCallGate.

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Preview.Domain.Grid.PreviewGridMarker
files.Summary:
Minimal grid marker used by preview + snapping/extents UI. Coordinates:

  • T: normalized position along wall length [0,1]

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Preview.Domain.Opening.PreviewOpening
files.Summary:
Minimal opening rectangle projection used by preview + extents interval logic. Coordinates:

  • T0/T1: normalized along wall length [0,1]
  • Y0/Y1: feet above wall base

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.Preview.Selection.PreviewSegmentSelection
files.Summary: Identifies a preview selection (girt or opening-role segment) for highlight rendering. For girts, SegmentIndex is the segment index within the girt's preview segments; when null, the selection refers to the whole girt member (all segments). For opening members, SegmentIndex is the index within opening.GetEffectiveConfigs(role).

files.Title: DBTools.SGT.Features.WallAnalysis.Domain.IWallAnalysisPlanBuilder
